bandReport.notes: Footers read and recorded: '( 45 - A )' and '( 47 - A )', both with 'TFDD-B-AGT' at foot left. Series A on both -- correct booklet. THE PAPER ENDS AT Q150: Q150's option (d) is the last printed content on p47, followed by white space and the footer, and PDF idx 24 (the next image) is a Centurion Defence Academy advertisement, confirmed by rendering it. SEAM p43 -> p45 IS CLEAN: p43 carries Q135-Q140 and Q140 is COMPLETE there (all four options print at the foot of its right column), so no question straddles the boundary and nothing between bands is unowned. No diagram or figure anywhere on either page -- every question is pure text. A Devanagari sliver shows at the left edge of both pages (the facing Hindi versos, printed 44 and 46); ignored per the brief. Candidate pen marks present and ignored. All 40 options were read label by label off the page, never copied between questions, including the four questions that share the I only / II only / Both / Neither and I,II,III / ...only option families. METHOD NOTE: the right column of p45 sits under the red watermark, so those questions were re-read from the NATIVE embedded raster through its RED CHANNEL, in which the pink watermark washes out while the near-neutral text survives; that removed the watermark entirely and is what the p45 Q144-Q146 readings rest on.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Green Nobel' :
I. It is given every alternate year.
II. In 2026, six winners were chosen and one of the winners is from Asia.
III. All the winners of 2026 are women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.subtopic: Civilian Awards, Honours and Educational Institutions
flags: YEAR DIGITS ARE SOFT. Statements II and III both print a year; the red watermark crosses it and the photograph is defocused there. Read as 2026 in BOTH, consistently, after the red-channel de-watermark pass on the native raster; the third and fourth digits are the uncertain ones and 2025 cannot be fully excluded. Corroborating but not decisive: Q146 and Q147 on these same pages both carry 2026 and this is the NDA II 2026 sitting.

SUBTOPIC is a close rather than exact fit: the 'Green Nobel' is an international environmental prize, not a civilian honour or an educational institution, but that subtopic is the only one in the catalog for awards.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding Exercise DUSTLIK-2026 :
I. It is a joint military exercise between India and U.A.E.
II. Its aim is to foster military cooperation and enhance combined capabilities to execute joint operations in semi-mountainous terrain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.subject: Current Affairs
flags: TRANSCRIBED AS PRINTED, NOT REPAIRED: statement I names 'India and U.A.E.'. DUSTLIK is the India-Uzbekistan exercise, so this is very likely the question's own testable falsehood; either way it is what the page says and it must not be corrected.
Punctuation read: a dot is clearly visible after the 'U'; the dot between 'A' and 'E' merges into the E's serif. Written 'U.A.E.' on that evidence.

questions.stem:

II. Advanced fighter aircraft of the Indian Air Force, including Rafale, HAL Tejas and Mirage 2000 carried out strikes.
III. Boeing Apache and Boeing Chinook helicopters participated in this exercise.
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.subject: Current Affairs
flags: SUBTOPIC forced on the qualifier: Vayu Shakti is a single-service Indian Air Force firepower demonstration, so it is neither bilateral nor multilateral, but 'Military Exercises — Bilateral and Multilateral' is the only exercise subtopic in the catalog.
Quoting is inconsistent in the printed question and is preserved: the stem writes 'Vayu Shakti-2026' inside single quotes, statement I writes it unquoted.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements related to water governance is/are correct ?
I. River Basin Management (RBM) is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India.
II. The major objectives of the RBM Scheme focus on promoting the use of water for domestic use.
III. The Brahmaputra Board is one of the key implementing agencies of the RBM.
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.subtopic: Governance, Policy and Union Territory Reform
flags: FORCED SUBTOPIC. The question is about a Central Sector Scheme and its administering ministry and implementing agency; the chosen subtopic covers 'Governance, Policy' (the stem's own words are 'water governance') but the 'Union Territory Reform' half does not apply. The alternative considered and rejected was Geography / 'Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport' / 'Economic Sectors and Government Schemes', which fits the water-resources content but not the administrative content the question actually tests.
